category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough and consolidation never bridge to or from neighbouring lessons; no teacher line like 'tomorrow Cal teaches us a STANDARD unit (centimetre) that fixes the count problem' anywhere in lesson_01.
category_feedback.required_fix: In consolidation, add an explicit forward-bridge: e.g., 'Roo says — tomorrow we meet a STANDARD unit (centimetre) so EVERY classroom counts the same way.' Then mirror that in expanded_walkthrough.rationale to anchor the unit arc.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.rationale names a real trap (cubes-for-everything) but cites no research and recovery_moves = ['Use unit-choice chart.', 'Drill unit for size.', 'Show extreme cases'] is a flat list — no branching by what the diagnostic shows.
category_feedback.required_fix: Cite Sarama & Clements (2009) Learning Trajectories for length measurement (unit-choice / iteration trap), and split recovery_moves by diagnostic: (a) child can iterate but won't switch unit -> show 200-cube hallway extreme; (b) child can't iterate cleanly (gaps/overlaps) -> drop back to careful cube alignment before unit choice.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: lesson_specific_materials lists '60 cubes + 12 hand-span + 12 footprint per pair' and an 'Inverse Relationship' anchor chart — fine for prep days, but no NO-PAPER, NO-PURCHASE alternative is offered anywhere in differentiation or expanded_walkthrough.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add to differentiation a 'No-materials version': use HANDSPAN, FOOTSTEP, and FINGER-WIDTH directly on classroom objects — child measures their desk in finger-widths vs hand-spans vs forearms; no cubes or printed cards required. Make it explicit so a substitute teacher can run lesson_01 with zero prep.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Roo anchors minds_on and consolidation and 'I can' criteria are present, but there is no distinctive quotable refrain or sentence frame children chant back — consolidation.exit_routine is just a fill-in: 'My ___ is ___ cubes OR ___ hand-spans long.'
category_feedback.required_fix: Give Roo a memorable refrain that returns every lesson, e.g. 'SMALL unit, BIG count — BIG unit, small count!' as a call-and-response. Add it to consolidation.exit_routine and reference it in teacher_script so children chant it back. This must be reusable in lessons 2-5.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Inverse relationship is taught conceptually (cubes vs hand-spans, same pencil different counts) but children are never invited to INVENT or COMPARE strategies, and expanded_walkthrough names the trap in plain language only — no Sarama & Clements / Battista / Lehrer & Schauble framing.
category_feedback.required_fix: In action.steps add a 'Predict-then-measure' move: child PREDICTS the count for a hand-span before measuring, then compares with a partner who used cubes; share strategies in consolidation. In expanded_walkthrough.rationale name the misconception in research terms (Lehrer 2003 / Sarama & Clements 2009 length-measurement trajectory: unit iteration before unit choice).

summary: Pair 1 worksheet is solid (4) — three parts each map to a success criterion and Part 3 is a genuine transfer task. Lesson 1 clears Level 3 across the board but doesn't reach Level 4 on five categories: no forward-bridge to lesson 2, no research-cited trap with branched recovery, no no-materials alternative, no quotable Roo refrain, and no strategy-comparison or research-grounded framing of the inverse-relationship misconception. All blocking fixes are inside lesson_01.
